text:
incident-bot: Pager: streaming-tail-latency p99 > 2.5s for service=stream-proxy region=us-east-1 — incoming rate spike, multiple stalled SSE connections. alert_id=INC-20250601-02

alice: ack — I'm on it, switching to incident channel. pinging oncall.

ben: looking at grafana, p95 jumped to 800ms, p99 at ~3.2s. Dashboard: https://grafana.internal/redwood/stream-proxy?from=now-30m&to=now

carol: seeing lots of "write timeout after 30s" in proxy logs and repeated "client slow consumer" errors downstream. sample logs: ```
2025-06-01T03:12:17Z stream-proxy[proxy-12] WARN write failed: broken pipe (client id=cust-42)
2025-06-01T03:12:19Z stream-proxy[proxy-12] INFO backpressure applied, queue_length=512
2025-06-01T03:12:21Z origin[or-8] ERROR stalled chunk send: timeout=30000
```

ben: hypothesis: a small subset of clients not reading, causing connection buffers to pile up -> proxy backpressure -> increased tail latency for all streaming responses. Could be a spike in long-poll consumers or a regression in proxy keepalive handling.

alice: can we triage affected customer list quickly? @devon can you pull the top 10 customers by concurrent streaming connections in us-east-1?

devon: pulling now, query: `SELECT tenant_id, count(*) as conns FROM connections WHERE region='us-east-1' AND protocol='sse' GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY conns DESC LIMIT 10;` — returning 7 tenants > 500 conns, top one cust-42 at 2,100 conns.

carol: cust-42 matches logs. They have a known mobile SDK that doesn't ack fast sometimes. historical notes: https://internal.docs/redwood/cust-42-sdk-issue

ben: immediate mitigations I'd try: 1) reduce proxy write timeout to 10s, 2) enable aggressive per-connection drop for idle readers (drop after N buffered bytes), 3) scale proxy pool + enable circuit-breaker for misbehaving origins. Any objections?

alice: do plan A then B. Ben — can you make the config change and roll to canary? Keep traffic routing so that we don't impact other regions.

ben: doing canary now. `/deploy-bot deploy stream-proxy --image=stream-proxy:2025.06.01-rc2 --env=canary --set proxy.write_timeout_ms=10000 --set proxy.buffer_limit_bytes=524288`

deploy-bot: Deploy started by ben. Canary on 3 pods in us-east-1. Health checks enabled. Logs: https://logs.redwood/stream-proxy/canary/1748001234

carol: also opened a temporary routing rule to divert 20% of cust-42 traffic to a fallback non-streaming endpoint (polling) to reduce pressure. config: `route: /v1/stream -> fallback_mode=true if tenant==cust-42`

devon: handoff: I'm taking oncall for this incident from here. I'll monitor impact and coordinate customer comms.

devon: initial impact numbers: ~2.3k users saw increased lag in last 10m, p99 reduced from 3.2s to 1.1s on canary after config change. p95 now ~450ms. Still seeing some stalled connections but much improved.

alice: great progress. Please capture exact windows for SLO breach: when did p99 cross 2s and when recovered?

devon: timeline: 03:08 UTC — p99 crossed 2s. 03:18 UTC — canary deploy started. 03:23 UTC — p99 dropped under 2s. 03:30 UTC — additional routing fallback reduced error rate for cust-42 by 70%.

carol: quick customer impact assessment: affected tenants: cust-42 (high), cust-88 (medium), cust-7 (low). Estimated error budget burn: p95 SLO burned ~12% in 30m window, p99 burned ~40% for same window.

ben: follow-ups I want to runbook: - add client-level throttling heuristics - increase proxy buffer pruning aggressiveness - add a metric for "buffered_bytes_per_conn" and alert at >250KB per conn - test SDK consumer ACK behaviour in staging

alice: assign tasks: ben -> patch proxy to support pruning + buffered metric (PR #4621), carol -> customer comms + postmortem initial draft, devon -> runbook updates + follow-up on cust-42 SDK with SEs.

devon: creating incident ticket INC-20250601-02 and adding assignees. ETA for full RCA: EOD. Will also schedule an immediate postmortem meeting tomorrow 15:00 UTC.

carol: customer comms draft (short): "We observed elevated streaming latency and stalls in us-east-1 affecting SSE connections for a subset of customers. We mitigated by rolling a canary proxy config and routing fallback for the most impacted customer. Symptoms resolved for most users by 03:23 UTC. Root cause investigation is ongoing. We will share a full postmortem."

alice: thanks — please add link to incident ticket in Comm.

devon: note for runbook: if client backpressure > 200KB for > 2m, auto-apply fallback routing for that tenant and page SREs.

ben: merging canary to prod after smoke: `/deploy-bot promote stream-proxy --from=canary --to=prod --wait`

deploy-bot: Promote complete. 12 pods updated. No failed healthchecks.

alice: monitoring p95/p99 now for 30m window. Will leave this thread open until the postmortem is published. :thumbsup:

devon: closing oncall handoff note: incident status -> mitigated, monitoring. Follow-ups tracked in INC-20250601-02.

incident-bot: Incident INC-20250601-02 status updated: MITIGATED -> MONITORING by devon at 2025-06-01T04:05:12Z

carol: added links: runbook PR https://github.com/redwood/proxy/pull/4621, incident ticket https://tracker.redwood/INC-20250601-02, postmortem draft https://docs.redwood/incidents/INC-20250601-02-draft.md

ben: quick note: regression hypothesis still open — will run bisect across last two deploys for proxy image 2025.05.29 -> 2025.06.01 to verify.

alice: thanks team. If anything regresses, page the same channel.
